# Model and source

```{r model-meta, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
ui <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Murinova_2022_oxacillin"))
cat("* Citation: ", ui$reference, "\n", sep = "")
cat("* Description: ", ui$description, "\n", sep = "")
```

* Article: <https://doi.org/10.3390/antibiotics11121736>

This is a one-compartment intravenous oxacillin model fitted to sparse routine
therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM) data in adults treated for staphylococcal
infections. The authors parameterized it in the volume of distribution (`Vd`)
and the elimination rate constant (`Ke`) rather than in clearance; the only
retained covariate is the CKD-EPI eGFR on `Ke`. The model's purpose in the
paper is a Monte Carlo probability-of-target-attainment (PTA) analysis on the
**unbound** concentration, which showed that the labelled intermittent 0.5-h
infusions cannot hold unbound oxacillin above the MIC for the whole dosing
interval and that continuous infusion can.

# Population

`r ui$population$n_subjects` adults (14 male, 10 female) treated with
intravenous oxacillin for staphylococcal infection at the Military University
Hospital in Prague between June 2021 and June 2022 contributed
`r ui$population$n_observations` total plasma concentrations (24 troughs and 8
post-infusion peaks; 1.33 per patient) (Murinova 2022 Results 2, Table 1,
Methods 4.1). Median (IQR) age was 55 (45-72) years, body weight 84 (74-96) kg,
BMI 28 (23-33) kg/m2 and serum albumin 32 (26-37) g/L. Renal function was
preserved to moderately impaired: CKD-EPI eGFR 1.53 (0.98-1.71, range
0.59-2.10) mL/s/1.73 m2, i.e. about 92 (59-103, range 35-126) mL/min/1.73 m2.
Patients on renal replacement therapy or extracorporeal life support were
excluded. Infections were orthopedic (10), central nervous system (7), sepsis
(3) and other (4); 21 were methicillin-susceptible *Staphylococcus aureus*,
with a median MIC of 0.25 mg/L. Doses were 1-3 g every 4 h as 0.5-h infusions
(one patient received 3-h extended infusions).

Unbound oxacillin was measured by ultrafiltration in the same samples; median
plasma protein binding was 86% (IQR 83-88%, range 74-97%) and was not
associated with any tested covariate, including albumin.

```{r population, echo = FALSE}
pop <- ui$population
tibble::tibble(
  Field = names(pop),
  Value = vapply(pop, function(x) paste(as.character(x), collapse = "; "), character(1))
) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Model `population` metadata (Murinova 2022 Table 1 and Methods).")
```

# Source trace

Every value below is also carried as an in-file comment beside its `ini()`
entry in `inst/modeldb/specificDrugs/Murinova_2022_oxacillin.R`.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lvc` (Vd) | 11.2 L | Table 2, `Vd_pop` (R.S.E. 30.4%) |
| `lkel` (Ke at eGFR = 0) | 0.73 1/h | Table 2, `Ke_pop` (R.S.E. 26.1%) |
| `e_crcl_kel` | 0.3 per mL/s/1.73 m2 | Table 2, `beta_Ke_eGFR` (R.S.E. 50.8%) |
| `etalvc` | 0.7 SD -> 0.49 variance | Table 2, `omega_Vd`, under "Standard deviation of the random effects" |
| `etalkel` | 0.11 SD -> 0.0121 variance | Table 2, `omega_Ke`, same heading |
| `propSd` | 0.4 | Table 2, error model parameter `b`; Results 2.1 "A proportional error model" |
| `fu` | 0.14 | Results 2, median protein binding 86% (IQR 83-88%) |
| `Log(Vd) = log(Vd_pop) + eta_Vd` | n/a | Results 2.1, first equation |
| `Log(Ke) = log(Ke_pop) + beta_Ke_eGFR x eGFR + eta_Ke` | n/a | Results 2.1, second equation |
| `d/dt(central) = -kel * central` | n/a | Results 2.1 "one-compartmental model with linear elimination kinetics" |
| `CRCL / 60` unit conversion | n/a | Table 1 / Table 2 report eGFR in mL/s/1.73 m2; the canonical `CRCL` column is mL/min/1.73 m2 |
| `Cu = fu * Cc` | n/a | Methods 4.6: PTA evaluated on "unbound oxacillin plasma concentration" |

## The eGFR effect: printed equation versus prose

The paper describes the eGFR effect in two ways that do not agree exactly. The
Results 2.1 equation, which is Monolix's standard covariate form for a
log-normally distributed parameter, is exponential:
`Log(Ke) = log(Ke_pop) + beta x eGFR + eta_Ke`, i.e.
`Ke = 0.73 * exp(0.3 * eGFR)`. The abstract, Table 2 units and the Discussion
instead describe an additive effect, "Ke started at a baseline of 0.73 h-1 and
increased by 0.3 h-1 with each 1 mL/s/1.73 m2 of eGFR", and the Discussion's
worked example ("In patients with an eGFR of 1.5 mL/s/1.73 m2 ... the oxacillin
Ke was therefore 1.18 h-1, which corresponds to the elimination half-life of
0.6 h") uses that linear reading: 0.73 + 0.3 * 1.5 = 1.18.

The model encodes the printed equation. Across the cohort's eGFR range the two
readings differ by at most about 4%, and both reproduce the reported half-life
of 0.6 h:

```{r egfr-forms}
egfr_si <- c(0.59, 0.98, 1.5, 1.53, 1.71, 2.10)
ke_forms <- tibble::tibble(
  eGFR_mL_s = egfr_si,
  Ke_equation = 0.73 * exp(0.3 * egfr_si),
  Ke_prose = 0.73 + 0.3 * egfr_si
) |>
  mutate(
    pct_diff = 100 * (Ke_equation / Ke_prose - 1),
    t_half_equation = log(2) / Ke_equation
  )
ke_forms |>
  mutate(across(-eGFR_mL_s, \(x) round(x, 3))) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "eGFR (mL/s/1.73 m2)" = eGFR_mL_s,
    "Ke, printed equation (1/h)" = Ke_equation,
    "Ke, prose reading (1/h)" = Ke_prose,
    "% difference" = pct_diff,
    "t1/2, printed equation (h)" = t_half_equation
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Ke across Table 1's eGFR summary values under the two readings.")

# Deterministic algebra. The Discussion's t1/2 of 0.6 h at eGFR 1.5 holds
# under the encoded form (0.605 h); a wrong unit on eGFR (mL/min instead of
# mL/s) would give exp(0.3 * 90) and a t1/2 of essentially zero.
stopifnot(
  abs(ke_forms$t_half_equation[ke_forms$eGFR_mL_s == 1.5] - 0.6) < 0.05,
  all(abs(ke_forms$pct_diff) < 5)
)
```

The Monte Carlo replication of Table 3 below was run under both forms while
the model was prepared; the exponential form matched the published PTAs as
well as or slightly better than the linear one (for 1 g every 4 h, fT > MIC =
100% at MIC 0.25 mg/L, about 40% versus 35% against the published 41.5%), so
nothing in the paper's own simulations argues against the printed equation.

## Typical-value solve against the closed form

```{r closed-form}
mod <- readModelDb("Murinova_2022_oxacillin")

# Typical subject at the cohort median eGFR (1.53 mL/s/1.73 m2), one 1 g dose
# as a 0.5-h infusion.
typ_ev <- data.frame(
  id = 1L,
  time = c(0, seq(0.05, 8, by = 0.05)),
  evid = c(1L, rep(0L, 160)),
  amt = c(1000, rep(NA_real_, 160)),
  rate = c(2000, rep(NA_real_, 160)),
  cmt = "central",
  CRCL = 1.53 * 60
)
typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  rxode2::zeroRe(mod), events = typ_ev, rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12
) |>
  as.data.frame()

k_typ <- 0.73 * exp(0.3 * 1.53)
v_typ <- 11.2
closed <- with(typ, ifelse(
  time <= 0.5,
  2000 / (k_typ * v_typ) * (1 - exp(-k_typ * time)),
  2000 / (k_typ * v_typ) * (1 - exp(-k_typ * 0.5)) * exp(-k_typ * (time - 0.5))
))
rel_err <- max(abs(typ$Cc / closed - 1))
rel_err
# Same parameters on both sides, so the difference is integrator error only
# (measured around 1e-9 at these tolerances).
stopifnot(rel_err < 1e-6, all(abs(typ$Cu / typ$Cc - 0.14) < 1e-12))
```

# Virtual cohort

Individual data are not public. eGFR, the only retained covariate, is drawn by
inverting a piecewise-linear interpolation of Table 1's five-number summary
(min 0.59, Q1 0.98, median 1.53, Q3 1.71, max 2.10 mL/s/1.73 m2). The
quartiles are left-skewed (the median sits close to Q3), which a fitted
log-normal cannot reproduce; quantile interpolation matches every published
summary by construction.

```{r cohort}
# set.seed() fixes R's RNG (the covariate draw). rxode2's eta stream is
# partitioned per solver thread, so CI may draw different individuals; every
# Monte Carlo assertion below is on a cohort proportion or median with a bound
# at least 3 binomial standard errors wide.
set.seed(20221201)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20221201)

n_arm <- 200L # cap is 200 per arm

sample_from_quantiles <- function(n, q) {
  stats::approx(
    x = c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1), y = q,
    xout = stats::runif(n), rule = 2
  )$y
}
draw_egfr <- function(n) sample_from_quantiles(n, c(0.59, 0.98, 1.53, 1.71, 2.10))

egfr_check <- stats::median(draw_egfr(n_arm))
egfr_check
# A mis-entered quantile vector moves the median by tens of percent.
stopifnot(abs(egfr_check / 1.53 - 1) < 0.15)
```

```{r event-builder}
# IV-infusion events as a plain data frame. Observation rows use the ODE state
# `central`, never the observable `Cc`; covariates are columns of this frame.
make_events <- function(regimen, dose_mg, tau_h, dur_h, n, id0, obs_grid,
                        end_h = 48) {
  ids <- id0 + seq_len(n)
  subj <- tibble::tibble(id = ids, eGFR = draw_egfr(n)) |>
    mutate(CRCL = eGFR * 60)
  doses <- subj |>
    tidyr::crossing(time = seq(0, end_h - tau_h, by = tau_h)) |>
    mutate(evid = 1L, amt = dose_mg, rate = dose_mg / dur_h)
  obs <- subj |>
    tidyr::crossing(time = obs_grid) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, amt = NA_real_, rate = NA_real_)
  bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    mutate(cmt = "central", regimen = regimen) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}
```

# Simulation

## Total concentrations under the observed regimen (Figure 2)

Figure 2 of the paper is a VPC of the total plasma concentrations. The study
data are not available, so the figure below shows the model's prediction
interval (with residual error) for the most typical study regimen, 2 g every
4 h as a 0.5-h infusion, over the first day.

```{r vpc}
ev_obs <- make_events(
  "2 g q4h (0.5 h infusion)", 2000, 4, 0.5, n_arm, 0L,
  obs_grid = seq(0, 24, by = 0.1), end_h = 24
)
sim_obs <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = ev_obs, keep = "regimen") |>
  as.data.frame()

sim_obs |>
  group_by(time) |>
  summarise(
    p10 = stats::quantile(sim, 0.10),
    p50 = stats::quantile(sim, 0.50),
    p90 = stats::quantile(sim, 0.90),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, p50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = pmax(p10, 0.01), ymax = p90), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 24, by = 4)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "Total oxacillin (mg/L)",
    title = "2 g every 4 h, 0.5-h infusion",
    subtitle = "Median and 10th-90th percentiles including residual error, n = 200",
    caption = "Compare Figure 2 of Murinova 2022."
  )
```

## Unbound concentration profiles for the six simulated regimens (Figure 3)

```{r sim-regimens}
regimens <- tibble::tribble(
  ~regimen,                         ~dose_mg, ~tau_h, ~dur_h,
  "1 g q6h (0.5 h infusion)",       1000,     6,      0.5,
  "1 g q4h (0.5 h infusion)",       1000,     4,      0.5,
  "3 g q6h (0.5 h infusion)",       3000,     6,      0.5,
  "1 g q4h (3 h infusion)",         1000,     4,      3,
  "6 g/day (continuous infusion)",  6000,     24,     24,
  "12 g/day (continuous infusion)", 12000,    24,     24
)

# Steady state is reached well within the first 24 h (t1/2 at most about
# 1.1 h at the lowest Ke in the cohort), so the PTA window is 24-48 h.
pta_grid <- seq(24, 48, by = 0.05)
ev_reg <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(regimens)), function(i) {
  make_events(
    regimens$regimen[i], regimens$dose_mg[i], regimens$tau_h[i],
    regimens$dur_h[i], n_arm, (i - 1L) * n_arm, obs_grid = pta_grid
  )
}))
sim_reg <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = ev_reg, keep = "regimen") |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(regimen = factor(regimen, levels = regimens$regimen))
stopifnot(!anyNA(sim_reg$Cu))
```

```{r figure3, fig.height = 6}
sim_reg |>
  group_by(regimen, time) |>
  summarise(
    p05 = stats::quantile(Cu, 0.05),
    p50 = stats::quantile(Cu, 0.50),
    p95 = stats::quantile(Cu, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time - 24, p50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(0.25, 2), colour = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~regimen, ncol = 2) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 24, by = 6)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time within the steady-state day (h)", y = "Unbound oxacillin (mg/L)",
    title = "Steady-state unbound concentrations (median, 5th-95th percentile)",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 3 of Murinova 2022. Dashed lines: MIC 0.25 and 2 mg/L."
  )
```

# Replicating Table 3 -- probability of target attainment

A subject attains the target when its unbound concentration stays above the
MIC for 100% (or at least 50%) of the steady-state day. The paper simulated 500
replicates of its 24 patients in Simulx; here each regimen uses 200 virtual
patients, so each PTA carries a binomial standard error of up to 3.5
percentage points.

```{r pta}
pta_sub <- sim_reg |>
  filter(time < 48) |>
  group_by(regimen, id) |>
  summarise(
    ft_025 = mean(Cu > 0.25),
    ft_2 = mean(Cu > 2),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
pta_sim <- pta_sub |>
  group_by(regimen) |>
  summarise(
    sim_100_025 = 100 * mean(ft_025 >= 1),
    sim_100_2 = 100 * mean(ft_2 >= 1),
    sim_50_025 = 100 * mean(ft_025 >= 0.5),
    sim_50_2 = 100 * mean(ft_2 >= 0.5),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

pta_paper <- tibble::tibble(
  regimen = factor(regimens$regimen, levels = regimens$regimen),
  pub_100_025 = c(4.35, 41.52, 17.56, 95.30, 99.82, 99.97),
  pub_100_2 = c(0.05, 2.60, 0.64, 32.23, 69.95, 90.72),
  pub_50_025 = c(60.83, 60.25, 87.77, 99.93, 99.82, 99.97),
  pub_50_2 = c(5.55, 27.69, 27.48, 72.40, 69.95, 90.72)
)
pta_cmp <- left_join(pta_paper, pta_sim, by = "regimen")

pta_cmp |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 1))) |>
  dplyr::select(
    regimen, pub_100_025, sim_100_025, pub_100_2, sim_100_2,
    pub_50_025, sim_50_025, pub_50_2, sim_50_2
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Regimen" = regimen,
    "100%, 0.25: published" = pub_100_025,
    "100%, 0.25: simulated" = sim_100_025,
    "100%, 2: published" = pub_100_2,
    "100%, 2: simulated" = sim_100_2,
    "50%, 0.25: published" = pub_50_025,
    "50%, 0.25: simulated" = sim_50_025,
    "50%, 2: published" = pub_50_2,
    "50%, 2: simulated" = sim_50_2
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = paste(
    "PTA (%) by fT > MIC target (100% or 50%) and MIC (mg/L).",
    "Published values from Table 3 of Murinova 2022."
  ))
```

The headline conclusions reproduce: no 0.5-h infusion regimen reaches 90% PTA
for the optimal target, the 3-h extended infusion does so only at MIC
0.25 mg/L, and at MIC 2 mg/L only 12 g/day by continuous infusion clears 90%.
The fT > MIC = 100% columns and the continuous-infusion rows match closely.

The fT > MIC = 50% column for the 0.5-h infusion regimens does **not**
reproduce. The published values are internally inconsistent with a
steady-state PK simulation: Table 3 reports a lower PTA for 1 g every 4 h
(60.25%) than for 1 g every 6 h (60.83%) at MIC 0.25 mg/L, although the 4-h
regimen delivers 50% more drug and spends a larger fraction of every interval
above any given MIC. That ordering is impossible for any single set of
individual parameters, so the 50% column was probably derived differently
(for example over a non-steady-state window) in Simulx. These cells are shown
but not asserted.

```{r pta-assert}
row <- function(r) pta_cmp[pta_cmp$regimen == r, ]
ci12 <- row("12 g/day (continuous infusion)")
ci6 <- row("6 g/day (continuous infusion)")
ext <- row("1 g q4h (3 h infusion)")
std6 <- row("1 g q6h (0.5 h infusion)")

# Model-true values (from 24 x 500 closed-form replicates while preparing the
# model): CI 12 g MIC 2 ~ 92%, CI 6 g MIC 2 ~ 69%, extended MIC 0.25 ~ 98%,
# standard q6h MIC 0.25 ~ 2%. With n = 200 the binomial SE is at most 3.3
# points, so 12- and 15-point bounds sit more than 3 SE from each estimate,
# while a wrong eGFR unit, a variance/SD mix-up on Vd (0.7 vs 0.49), or a
# missing fu moves these by tens of points.
stopifnot(
  abs(ci12$sim_100_2 - ci12$pub_100_2) < 12,
  abs(ci6$sim_100_2 - ci6$pub_100_2) < 15,
  ext$sim_100_025 > 85,
  std6$sim_100_025 < 15,
  ci12$sim_100_2 > ci6$sim_100_2
)
```

## eGFR-graded continuous infusion

The paper's dosing proposal gives 9.5 g/day by continuous infusion for eGFR
0.5-1.0, 11 g/day for 1.0-1.5 and 12.5 g/day above 1.5 mL/s/1.73 m2, and
reports a pooled PTA of 90.18% for fT > MIC = 100% at MIC 2 mg/L.

```{r graded}
ev_graded <- make_events(
  "graded", 1, 24, 24, n_arm, 10000L, obs_grid = seq(24, 48, by = 0.5)
) |>
  mutate(
    daily_mg = case_when(eGFR <= 1.0 ~ 9500, eGFR <= 1.5 ~ 11000, TRUE ~ 12500),
    amt = ifelse(evid == 1L, daily_mg, NA_real_),
    rate = ifelse(evid == 1L, daily_mg / 24, NA_real_)
  )
sim_graded <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = ev_graded, keep = "daily_mg") |>
  as.data.frame()

pta_graded <- sim_graded |>
  filter(time < 48) |>
  group_by(id, daily_mg) |>
  summarise(ok = all(Cu > 2), .groups = "drop")
pta_graded_pct <- 100 * mean(pta_graded$ok)
c(simulated = pta_graded_pct, published = 90.18)
# Model-true ~ 90%; SE ~ 2.1 points at n = 200.
stopifnot(abs(pta_graded_pct - 90.18) < 10)
```

# PKNCA validation

A single 1 g dose as a 0.5-h infusion in the 200-subject cohort. The paper
reports no NCA; its only reported exposure summary is the Discussion's
elimination half-life of 0.6 h at eGFR 1.5 mL/s/1.73 m2, which is the
reference below (the cohort median eGFR is 1.53).

```{r pknca}
ev_sd <- make_events(
  "1 g single dose (0.5 h infusion)", 1000, 24, 0.5, n_arm, 20000L,
  obs_grid = c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8), end_h = 24
)
sim_sd <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  rxode2::zeroRe(mod, "sigma"), events = ev_sd, keep = "regimen"
) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::rename(treatment = regimen)

# Integrator undershoot near zero is noise; floor it, and keep the time-zero
# row so AUC is anchored at 0.
stopifnot(all(sim_sd$Cc >= -1e-6 * max(sim_sd$Cc)))
conc_sd <- sim_sd |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  mutate(Cc = pmax(Cc, 0)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
dose_sd <- ev_sd |>
  filter(evid == 1L) |>
  select(id, time, amt, treatment = regimen)

nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_sd, Cc ~ time | treatment + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_sd, amt ~ time | treatment + id),
  intervals = data.frame(
    start = 0, end = Inf,
    cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE
  )
))

nca_ref <- data.frame(
  treatment = "1 g single dose (0.5 h infusion)",
  half.life = 0.6
)
nca_tbl <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  nca_res, nca_ref,
  by = "treatment",
  params = "half.life",
  units = c(half.life = "h")
)
knitr::kable(nca_tbl, caption = "Median simulated NCA half-life vs. the Discussion's 0.6 h.")

nca_df <- as.data.frame(nca_res)
med_hl <- stats::median(nca_df$PPORRES[nca_df$PPTESTCD == "half.life"])
med_auc <- stats::median(nca_df$PPORRES[nca_df$PPTESTCD == "aucinf.obs"])
c(median_half_life_h = med_hl, median_aucinf_mg_h_L = med_auc)
# Median half-life: model-true about log(2) / (0.73 * exp(0.3 * 1.53)) = 0.60 h
# with only 11% IIV on Ke; robust to the draw.
stopifnot(abs(med_hl / 0.6 - 1) < 0.15)
```

```{r nca-summary}
nca_df |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "aucinf.obs", "half.life")) |>
  group_by(PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(
    median = stats::median(PPORRES),
    p05 = stats::quantile(PPORRES, 0.05),
    p95 = stats::quantile(PPORRES, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) signif(x, 3))) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "NCA parameter" = PPTESTCD,
    "Median" = median,
    "5th percentile" = p05,
    "95th percentile" = p95
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Single-dose NCA across the virtual cohort (1 g, 0.5-h infusion).")
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **eGFR effect form.** The printed Results 2.1 equation
  (`Log(Ke) = log(Ke_pop) + beta x eGFR + eta`, exponential) is encoded. The
  prose, Table 2 units and the Discussion's worked example (Ke 1.18 1/h at
  eGFR 1.5) read the same coefficient as an additive 0.3 1/h per mL/s/1.73 m2.
  Within the cohort's eGFR range the two readings differ by under 5%; see
  *The eGFR effect* above.
* **eGFR units.** The paper reports eGFR in mL/s/1.73 m2; the model takes the
  canonical `CRCL` in mL/min/1.73 m2 and divides by 60. The effect is
  uncentered, so `lkel` is Ke at eGFR = 0, not a typical value.
* **Random effects.** Table 2 reports the random effects as standard
  deviations (0.7 on Vd, 0.11 on Ke); they are squared to variances. The
  0.7 SD on Vd is large (CV about 80%) and reflects sparse, trough-dominated
  sampling (24 of 32 samples were troughs).
* **Unbound fraction.** `fu = 0.14` is the cohort median of the measured
  protein binding (86%) and is fixed for every subject. The paper does not
  state how unbound concentrations were generated in Simulx; a fixed median
  fraction is the simplest reading and reproduces the continuous-infusion PTAs.
  Measured binding ranged from 74% to 97%, so an individual's unbound exposure
  can differ from `Cu` by roughly a factor of two either way.
* **Covariate distribution.** eGFR is drawn from Table 1's five-number summary
  by quantile interpolation; the individual values are not published.
* **PTA definition.** fT > MIC is evaluated on the unbound concentration
  without residual error over the second (steady-state) day. The fT > MIC = 50%
  column for the 0.5-h infusion regimens of Table 3 does not reproduce and
  appears internally inconsistent (see above).
* **Errata.** No erratum or correction for this article was found (checked
  2026-10-10).
